answer.worked:
Reflect in both axes by replacing $x$ by $-x$ and $y$ by $-y$.
$$\begin{align*}-y&=(-x)(1+\sin(-x))\\-y&=-x(1-\sin x)\\y&=x(1-\sin x)\end{align*}$$
Each point $(x,y)$ maps to $(-x,-y)$. The contact at $(\frac{3\pi}{2},0)$ becomes $(-\frac{3\pi}{2},0)$, and the origin remains fixed. The large positive hump becomes the large negative trough.
